candidate.answerReason: Mike's bill was 20 dollars and Joe's was 10 dollars, so the difference was 10 dollars.

methods.label: Recover each whole bill
methods.explanation:
Mike's \(10\%\) tip is \(\frac1{10}\) of his bill. His \(2\)-dollar tip is therefore one of ten equal parts of the bill, so his bill was \(10\cdot2=20\) dollars.

Joe's \(20\%\) tip is \(\frac15\) of his bill. His bill was therefore \(5\cdot2=10\) dollars.

The difference between their bills was \(20-10=10\) dollars, choice D.
methods.levelReason: Simple percentage-to-fraction conversions and equal-share reasoning recover the unknown bills.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is finding an original amount from a known percentage of it. Converting the two percentages to unit fractions supports the written method, and recovering a whole from a fractional part supplies the underlying quantitative relationship.
